title: Alphabet
body:
A finite, non-empty set of symbols, written $\Sigma$. That is the whole definition.

$\Sigma = \{0, 1\}$ and $\Sigma = \{a, b, c\}$ are the two you see in every example. Sequences
of symbols from $\Sigma$ are [[Strings]]; sets of those strings are [[Languages]].

Note it is the *input* alphabet. A [[Turing Machine]] also has a tape alphabet $\Gamma$ with
$\Sigma \subseteq \Gamma$, which additionally contains the blank symbol $\sqcup$.

[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]]
